# Session Start with Beads

## Overview
Check beads state BEFORE skill selection. Beads determines WHAT to work on, skills determine HOW.

## Protocol

1. Check bd state:
   ```bash
   bd ready --json
   bd list --status in_progress --json
   ```

2. If in_progress exists:
   - Run: bd show <id>
   - Read notes field (COMPLETED/IN PROGRESS/NEXT/BLOCKERS)
   - Report: "Continuing [title]. Last session: [COMPLETED]. Next: [NEXT]"
   - Ask: "Continue with this, or work on something else?"

3. If nothing in_progress but items ready:
   - Run: bv --robot-plan
   - Present top 3 suggestions to user
   - Ask: "Which would you like to work on? Or something else?"

4. If user selects or confirms:
   - Mark chosen issue in_progress: bd update <id> --status in_progress

5. THEN check relevant skills for HOW to do the work

## Reference
For bd/bv commands: ~/.claude/skills/beads/, ~/.claude/skills/using-bv/

title: Create multi-agent-coordination skill
description:
WHAT: Create new skill at skills/multi-agent-coordination/SKILL.md to replace git-worktrees for concurrent agent work.

WHY: Git worktrees complicate beads state management. Beads provides better coordination - agents claim tasks atomically, work on same branch.

HOW:
Create skills/multi-agent-coordination/SKILL.md with:

---
name: multi-agent-coordination
description: Use when multiple agents need to work concurrently - coordinates via beads task claims instead of git worktrees
---

# Multi-Agent Coordination

## Overview
Agents coordinate via beads status instead of separate git worktrees. This keeps beads state unified and avoids merge complexity.

## How Agents Coordinate

1. Check available work:
   ```bash
   bd ready --json
   bd list --status in_progress --json
   ```

2. Claim work atomically:
   ```bash
   bd update <task-id> --status in_progress
   ```
   
3. Other agents see claimed work and pick different tasks

4. Work on same branch
   - Beads tasks are granular enough to touch different files
   - No merge conflicts because different tasks = different code

## Preventing Conflicts

If two tasks would modify the same file:
```bash
bd dep add <task-a-id> <task-b-id> --type blocks
```

This ensures they run sequentially, not concurrently.

## Using bv for Planning

```bash
bv --robot-plan  # Shows which tasks can be parallelized
```

Tasks without blocking dependencies can run concurrently.

## Advantages Over Git Worktrees

| Worktrees | Beads Coordination |
|-----------|-------------------|
| Separate .beads/ per worktree | Single source of truth |
| Merge complexity | No merges needed |
| Branch management overhead | Same branch |
| State divergence risk | State always unified |

## When This Doesn't Work

If tasks truly need isolated environments (different dependencies, conflicting configs), use separate checkouts instead of worktrees, and coordinate manually.

## Reference
For bd/bv commands: ~/.claude/skills/beads/, ~/.claude/skills/using-bv/

CONTEXT:
- Replaces using-git-worktrees skill for beads workflows
- Key insight: beads task granularity provides natural isolation
- Atomic task claiming prevents race conditions
- Same branch = simpler CI/CD

- [ ] Shows how to prevent conflicts with blocks dependency

title: Create beads-checkpoint skill
description:
WHAT: Create new skill at skills/beads-checkpoint/SKILL.md

WHY: Formalize checkpointing protocol so notes are written BEFORE context is lost to compaction.

HOW:
Create skills/beads-checkpoint/SKILL.md with:

---
name: beads-checkpoint
description: Use at 70%+ token usage or before context switch to preserve work state in beads for compaction survival
---

# Beads Checkpoint

## Overview
Write structured notes to beads BEFORE compaction happens. Notes written after context loss are low quality.

## Checkpoint Triggers

| Trigger | Action |
|---------|--------|
| 70% token usage | Proactive checkpoint (best quality) |
| 85% token usage | Warning, checkpoint immediately |
| 90% token usage | Emergency auto-checkpoint |
| Major milestone | Update notes with progress |
| Hit a blocker | Capture what was tried |
| Task transition | Update before switching |

## Protocol

1. List in-progress issues:
   bd list --status in_progress --json

2. For each, write structured notes:
   bd update <id> --notes "COMPLETED: [specific deliverables, not vague]
   IN PROGRESS: [current state + immediate next step]
   NEXT: [concrete action]
   BLOCKERS: [what's preventing progress, if any]
   KEY DECISIONS: [important context with rationale]"

3. Commit beads state:
   git add .beads/
   git commit -m "chore: checkpoint beads state"
   (Ask user before committing per CLAUDE.md)

## Quality Check
Before checkpointing, ask: "If a fresh agent started with ONLY these notes, could they continue effectively?"

If no -> Add more context.

## Reference
For bd commands: ~/.claude/skills/beads/

CONTEXT:
- Precompact hook is too late - by then context is already degraded
- 70% is ideal checkpoint point with full context available
- Structured format (COMPLETED/IN PROGRESS/NEXT) survives compaction well

ACCEPTANCE:
- [ ] File created at skills/beads-checkpoint/SKILL.md
- [ ] Trigger table shows all checkpoint scenarios
- [ ] Protocol is clear step-by-step
- [ ] Quality check question included
- [ ] References beads skill

title: Create plan-to-beads skill
description:
WHAT: Create new skill at skills/plan-to-beads/SKILL.md that replaces writing-plans for beads-integrated workflows.

WHY: This is the KEY change - instead of markdown implementation plans, we create granular, self-documenting beads. Each bead should be self-contained enough for a fresh agent to implement.

HOW:
Create skills/plan-to-beads/SKILL.md with:

---
name: plan-to-beads
description: Use after brainstorming to convert approved design into granular, self-documenting beads with full dependency structure
---

# Plan to Beads

## Overview
Convert approved design document into comprehensive beads structure. Each bead must be self-contained - a fresh agent with ONLY that bead should understand what to do and why.

## Process

### 1. Read the Design Document
Understand: goals, architecture decisions, components, constraints.

### 2. Create Epic
```bash
bd create "Feature: [name]" -t epic -p [priority] --json
bd update <epic-id> --description "[Full context from design]
Goal: [what we're building and why]
Architecture: [key decisions and rationale]
Design doc: docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md
Success criteria: [what done looks like]"
```

### 3. Decompose into Granular Tasks
For each logical unit of work:
```bash
bd create "[Specific task]" -t task --json
bd dep add <epic-id> <task-id> --type parent-child
```

### 4. Task Description Format (CRITICAL)
Each task MUST include:

WHAT: Specific deliverable
WHY: How it serves the goal
HOW: Implementation approach
CONTEXT: Background, constraints, considerations
ACCEPTANCE:
- [ ] Criterion 1
- [ ] Criterion 2

### 5. Add Dependency Structure
```bash
# Task B requires Task A to complete first
bd dep add <task-a-id> <task-b-id> --type blocks

# Tasks that are children of epic
bd dep add <epic-id> <child-id> --type parent-child
```

### 6. Verify Structure
```bash
bv --robot-plan  # Should show logical execution order
bv --robot-insights  # Check for cycles
```

### 7. Quality Check
For each bead, ask: "Could a fresh agent with ONLY this bead implement it correctly?"
If no -> Add more context to description.

## What NOT to Create
- Don't create markdown implementation plans (use beads instead)
- Don't duplicate design doc content (reference it)
- Don't create vague tasks ("implement auth" is too vague)
- Don't skip WHY and CONTEXT

## Reference
For bd/bv commands: ~/.claude/skills/beads/, ~/.claude/skills/using-bv/

CONTEXT:
- This replaces the writing-plans skill for beads workflows
- Key insight: beads ARE the implementation plan, not a separate artifact
- Each bead is self-documenting for compaction survival
- User wants granular beads (one per implementation step)

## Beads Integration

This fork integrates with [Beads](https://github.com/steveyegge/beads) for persistent task tracking across sessions.

### Requirements

- Beads CLI (`bd`) installed
- Beads Viewer (`bv`) for planning suggestions
- User skills at `~/.claude/skills/beads/` and `~/.claude/skills/using-bv/`

### New Workflow

1. **Session Start** - Checks `bd ready` and `bd list --status in_progress` BEFORE skill selection
2. **Brainstorming** - Creates design doc AND bd epic
3. **Plan to Beads** - Converts design to granular, self-documenting beads (replaces markdown plans)
4. **Execution** - Driven by bd tasks, updates status throughout
5. **Code Review** - Verifies bd acceptance criteria
6. **Completion** - Closes bd issues, commits .beads/

### Key Differences from Base Superpowers

| Base Superpowers | With Beads |
|-----------------|------------|
| Markdown implementation plans | Beads track implementation |
| TodoWrite for all tracking | TodoWrite for session, Beads for persistence |
| Git worktrees for isolation | Beads coordination for multi-agent |
| Auto-commits | Asks before committing |

### New Skills

- **session-start-with-beads** - Session start protocol
- **plan-to-beads** - Convert design to granular beads
- **beads-checkpoint** - Compaction survival
- **multi-agent-coordination** - Replace git-worktrees

### Deprecated Skills

- **writing-plans** - Use plan-to-beads instead
- **using-git-worktrees** - Use multi-agent-coordination instead

Update workflow diagram to show beads integration.

- README is the first thing users see
- Must be clear about requirements and changes

title: Clarify TDD delete vs discard
description:
WHAT: Update skills/test-driven-development/SKILL.md to clarify "delete" means "discard uncommitted work" not "delete files."

WHY: User's CLAUDE.md says never delete files without permission. TDD skill says "delete code written before tests." These appear to conflict but are about different things.

HOW:
Changes to TDD skill:

1. Change wording throughout:
   - "Delete it" -> "Discard it"
   - "Delete means delete" -> "Discard means discard"

2. Add clarification box after "Delete means delete" section:

```markdown
**Clarification:** "Discard" means revert uncommitted changes, not delete files.

If you've written implementation code before writing tests:
- Use `git checkout <file>` to revert changes
- Or `git stash` if you want to reference later
- Do NOT use `rm` to delete files

The principle: Don't keep the implementation in your head while writing tests. Start fresh so tests drive the design.
```

3. Update red flags list:
   - "Keep as reference" -> still a red flag, but clarify the solution is git stash/checkout, not file deletion

CONTEXT:
- CLAUDE.md: "You may NOT delete any file or directory unless I explicitly give the exact command"
- TDD skill is about discarding uncommitted work, not file deletion
- The spirit is the same: don't let pre-test code influence test design
- Just need clearer wording to avoid confusion

ACCEPTANCE:
- [ ] "Delete" changed to "discard" throughout
- [ ] Clarification box added explaining this means git checkout/stash
- [ ] No references to rm or file deletion
- [ ] Spirit of TDD preserved (don't keep pre-test code)

title: Fix commit policy (ask before committing)
description:
WHAT: Update all skills to ask before committing instead of auto-committing.

WHY: User's CLAUDE.md says: "Only create commits when requested by the user." Superpowers auto-commits in several places.

HOW:

3. skills/subagent-driven-development/SKILL.md
   - Same pattern - ask before commit

4. skills/finishing-a-development-branch/SKILL.md

Pattern to use:
```
"Ready to commit? Changes:
- [file1]: [brief description]
- [file2]: [brief description]

Commit message: [proposed message]
```

CONTEXT:

title: End-to-end workflow test
description:
WHAT: Test the complete integrated workflow from session start to feature completion.

WHY: Must verify all pieces work together before declaring integration complete.

HOW:
Test scenario: Implement a small feature using the full workflow

1. Session Start
   - Verify bd ready/in_progress check happens
   - Verify bv --robot-plan suggestions shown
   - Verify skill selection happens AFTER beads check

2. Brainstorming
   - Create a simple design
   - Verify design doc created in docs/plans/
   - Verify bd epic created
   - Verify commit asks for permission

3. Plan to Beads
   - Run plan-to-beads on the design
   - Verify granular tasks created
   - Verify dependencies set correctly
   - Verify bv --robot-plan shows logical order

4. Execution
   - Execute a task
   - Verify bd task marked in_progress
   - Verify TodoWrite created for session
   - Verify bd task closed on completion
   - Verify commit asks permission

5. Code Review
   - Run code-reviewer
   - Verify acceptance criteria checked
   - Verify Beads Status in output

6. Completion
   - Finish the feature
   - Verify all bd tasks closed
   - Verify epic closed
   - Verify .beads/ committed

7. Checkpoint Test
   - Simulate high token usage
   - Verify checkpoint behavior triggers
   - Verify notes are useful for resume

CONTEXT:
- This validates the entire integration
- Should find any gaps or rough edges
- Use a real (small) feature, not a mock

ACCEPTANCE:
- [ ] Full workflow tested end-to-end
- [ ] All beads integration points verified
- [ ] Commit policy respected throughout
- [ ] No errors or unexpected behavior
- [ ] Notes are sufficient for session resume
